parsed.rationale: Both `HSBColor.uiColor` (line 53) and `HSBColor.nsColor` (line 63) live in the same file (`Shared/ColorPalette/Sources/ColorPalette/HSBColor.swift`) and share a Jaccard similarity of 0.714, indicating nearly identical bodies that differ only in the platform color type they instantiate. Because both properties are already co-located in the same type and package (`ColorPalette`), extraction to a common location is moot; the right fix is to factor out the shared HSB component arithmetic into a private helper or to unify the two properties behind a platform-conditional `PlatformColor` typealias. No restraint markers are present, so the duplication is unintentional and worth addressing.

specifics.proposed_action: Introduce a private helper method on `HSBColor` (e.g., `func makeColor(usingUIKit: Bool) -> <PlatformColor>` or a shared `func colorComponents() -> (hue: CGFloat, saturation: CGFloat, brightness: CGFloat, alpha: CGFloat)`) that encapsulates the shared HSB-to-platform-color conversion logic. Both `uiColor` and `nsColor` then delegate to this helper, differing only in which platform type they construct (`UIColor` vs `NSColor`). Alternatively, use a `#if canImport(UIKit) / canImport(AppKit)` typealias (`typealias PlatformColor = UIColor / NSColor`) and collapse both properties into a single `var color: PlatformColor` computed property, eliminating the duplication entirely.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: Neither `generic-parameterization` nor `extract-to-common` fits cleanly: the two properties are already in the same file and same type (`HSBColor`) within the same package (`ColorPalette`), so there is nothing to extract or move. The divergence is purely in the *return type* (`UIColor` vs `NSColor`), not in a type parameter that can be abstracted away with a generic. A `default-implementation` pattern does not apply because there is no protocol involved. The most idiomatic Swift resolution is either a shared private helper or a platform-conditional typealias collapse — neither of which maps to the named categories.
